title: Expires must not be in the past

spec.name: RFC 9116
spec.normative_quote: The "Expires" field indicates the date and time after which the data contained in the "security.txt" file is considered stale and should not be used (as per Section 5.3).
spec.note: Verified against a live fetch of https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9116.txt on 2026-07-30. Corrects a prior defect: the second sentence ('Consumers of a security.txt file whose Expires date has passed SHOULD consider its contents stale') was fabricated -- no such consumer-facing SHOULD exists anywhere in RFC 9116; §5.3 (referenced by the real first sentence) addresses producers, not consumers. See policy_note for why this rule still fails at severity: fail despite the RFC imposing no explicit consumer obligation.

policy_note: RFC 9116 does not mandate any particular consumer behavior toward an expired security.txt (see note). Failing this rule at severity: fail is our own operational judgment -- an Expires date in the past signals the file's contents (including Contact) may be stale, and treating that as a hard failure is a reasonable, defensible inference from the RFC's stated purpose for the field, not a claim that the RFC itself requires it.
applicability: A security.txt body containing a parseable Expires: value.
expectation: The parsed Expires instant is not earlier than the evaluation instant.

cases.name: Expires in the future -- this rule does not fire
